This petition is filed by the petitioners/accused Nos.4 and 5 under Section 482 of Cr.P.C for quashing the criminal proceedings in Slp.C.C.No.872/2022 on the file of the L Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru (CCH-51) for the offence punishable under Sections 10 and 11 of Prohibition of Child Marriage Act.

sentences.text: 2. During the pendency of this petition, both petitioners/accused Nos.4 and 5 and respondent No.2 have filed a joint compromise petition for seeking permission of this Court to compound the above case and acquit the petitioners in Special C.C.No.872/2022 for the aforesaid offences.

3. Heard learned counsel appearing for the petitioners and learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2.
4.
The case of the petitioners is that respondent No.2 said to be married accused No.1 and accused Nos.2 and 3 are the parents-in-law.
Their marriage was performed by the petitioners in the year 2009 when she was minor.

Thereafter, there was a dispute arisen Smt Tulasi C vs The State Of Karnataka on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91727920/

sentences.text: Therefore, respondent No.2 filed a complaint against the husband and parents-in-law for the offence punishable under Sections 376(B), 498(A) read with 34 of IPC in Crime No.145/2018.

During the course of investigation, the police have filed charge sheet against the parents of the victim on the ground that the parents have performed the marriage of the minor girl, which is punishable under Sections 10 and 11 of Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006.

5. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, wherein the petitioners are the parents of respondent No.2 and she was aged 25 years at the time of filing the compliant in the year 2013 and the marriage said to be held in the year 2009 and in view of the settlement arrived between the parties and the petitioners and respondent No.2 is living together in one house and respondent No.2 is litigating the case against accused Nos.1 to 3 i.e., husband and parents-in-law for the offence punishable under Sections 498(A) and 376(B) of IPC, I.A.No.2/2023 needs to be allowed.

Consequently, the criminal petition is allowed and the proceedings in Special C.C.No.872/2022 and the order dated 04.07.2019 on the file of the L Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru (CCH-51) is hereby quashed.
